question.text: One year after Stonewall, the first of these public events took place. These events celebrate the progress of the LGBT community and often feature people waving rainbow flags as they march down streets.
question.answerHtml: Pride parades (accept additional information, such as Gay Pride parades; prompt on partial answers)
question.clue: The largest annual one of these events in the world first started in New York after the Stonewall Riots and attracted 4 million visitors in 2019. These events express solidarity with the LGBTQ+ community.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about tragic events concerning a certain family.
swap.text: During the 1968 California primaries, Sirhan Sirhan shot and killed this brother of JFK in a hotel.
swap.clue: This man formed a team to investigate Jimmy Hoffa, the head of the Teamsters Union.

question.leadin: This man declared "segregation now, segregation tomorrow, segregation forever," then tried to back that up by standing in the door to block two black students from entering his state's university in Tuscaloosa.
question.text: Name this politician. His wife, Lurleen, ran for governor when he was term-limited in 1966.
question.clue: During this man's 1972 presidential run with former Air Force general Curtis LeMay, he was shot and paralyzed by Arthur Bremer.

swap.text: As president, Johnson launched this series of programs that included Medicare and Medicaid. Its most famous part was the "War on Poverty" that led to the Economic Opportunity Act.
swap.clue: One act under this program significantly boosted public education funding, while another created the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

question.leadin: Answer the following about African-American history referenced in Angie Thomas's novel The Hate U Give.
question.text: In the Carters' house, a photo of this man wielding a rifle and peering out of his window hangs beside a painting of Black Jesus. The Black Panther reading list contains this civil rights activist's autobiography, which was finished by Alex Haley after his 1965 assassination.
question.clue: This founder of Muslim Mosque, Inc. and the Organization of Afro-American Unity was assassinated at the Audubon Ballroom.

swap.leadin: This movement began in December 1955 and ended in December 1956.
swap.text: Name this large scale protest that aimed to cripple a public transportation system in a namesake city in Alabama.
swap.clue: This event was ended with the decision made in Browder v Gayle, and the Southern Christian Leadership Conference was founded by Martin Luther King Jr. shortly after this event.

question.text: This Senator criticized Rustin as a "Communist, draft-dodger, and homosexual" and entered his Pasadena arrest file into record. This Dixiecrat once delivered a 24-hour filibuster in opposition to the Civil Rights Act of 1957.
question.clue: After claiming that the U.S. would have been a better place had this man been president, Trent Lott resigned as Senate majority leader; Lott made those remarks in 2002 at this senator's 100th birthday party.

swap.leadin: Name some landmark U.S. court cases.
swap.text: This 1963 case dealt with a Florida man convicted of breaking into the Bay Harbor Pool Room and ruled that not giving a convicted felon a right to counsel was unconstitutional.
swap.clue: Future Supreme Court Justice Abe Fortas was appointed to represent the plaintiff in this case, who was arrested in Panama City, Florida for breaking into a pool hall.

question.text: After the management at Constitution Hall refused to allow her to sing, Eleanor Roosevelt and Secretary of the Interior Harold Ickes arranged a free concert at the Lincoln Memorial where an audience of 75,000 gathered.

swap.leadin: This event started after the motorist Marquette Frye was pulled over by a cop for drunk driving.
swap.text: Name these riots which took place in a namesake neighborhood for about a week in August, 1965.
swap.clue: The McCone Report was commissioned by Governor Pat Brown to investigate this event, which began when Marquette Frye was arrested for drunk driving.

question.leadin: This case was decided with Briggs v. Elliott and has two parts, the second of which commanded action be taken "with all deliberate speed."
question.text: Name this Supreme Court case that overturned Plessy v. Ferguson in 1954 and 1955. This case also featured future justice Thurgood Marshall as the chief counsel for the NAACP.
question.answerHtml: Brown v. Board of Education [or Oliver L. Brown et. al v. The Board of Education of Topeka, et. al]
question.clue: This case's decision cited an experiment in which children were asked to choose between dolls by Kenneth and Mamie Clark.

swap.text: The Compton's Cafeteria Riot preceded this event, which began with a police raid at the namesake Greenwich Village establishment. These 1969 riots at a New York gay bar helped launch the gay rights movement.
swap.clue: Howard Smith and Lucian Truscott covered this event in The Village Voice, during which folk singer Dave Van Ronk was arrested by Seymour Pine.

question.leadin: Workers in this industry striked under the slogan "I AM a Man."
question.text: Name this industry, whose workers began striking in response to the deaths of Echol Cole and Robert Walker. Martin Luther King Jr. was in Memphis supporting the strike in this industry in 1968 when he was assassinated.
question.answerHtml: sanitation industry [or garbagemen; or any other answers suggesting garbage collection; or Memphis sanitation strike]
question.clue: This industry's use of "wiener barrel" trucks declined after Echol Cole and Robert Walker's deaths triggered a strike that popularized the slogan "I AM A MAN."

swap.leadin: Sixteen-year old Larry Kayne was shot for marching in support of this event.
swap.text: Identify this 1968 event that began after the deaths of Echol Cole and Robert Walker. An activist delivered the "I've Been to the Mountaintop" speech in support of this event at Mason Temple one day before his assassination.
swap.clue: This event during which a group of predominantly African American workers walked off the job, much to the chagrin of Mayor Henry Loeb, a "white unity" advocate.

question.leadin: While Ambassador to India, this man gave the "world's largest check" to Indira Gandhi.
question.text: Name this man who, while Assistant Secretary of Labor in 1965, produced a controversial namesake report claiming that the relative absence of nuclear families was a major factor in the creation of black poverty.
question.clue: This man identified what he called a "matriarchy" in one group by looking at Department of Labor statistics in a document that was criticized byWilliam Ryan in a book that coined the term "blaming the victim."

swap.leadin: In 1964, three members of this organization were brutally murdered in Neshoba County, Mississippi.
swap.text: Name this civil rights organization that, as a part of the COFO, led the campaign to register African-American voters in Mississippi in Freedom Summer. This organization's founding Chicago chapter desegregated White City Roller Rink and fought overcrowding and double-shifts in public schools.
swap.clue: Its second director retired in order to design a planned town called Soul City in North Carolina which quickly fell through.

question.text: The Green Book helped develop this network of theaters and nightclubs catering to black audiences in the South. Similar to the Jewish Borscht Belt, it launched the careers of B.B. King, Ray Charles, and Marvin Gaye.
question.clue: During Jim Crow, black performers traveled to nightclubs such as the Uptown Theatre in Philadelphia that were part of this informal set of venues, whose name is a play on the Borscht Belt.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about affirmative action in the United States.
swap.text: This 2003 case held that the University of Michigan had violated the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment by giving minority applicants points because of their race.

question.leadin: Critics of this legislation asked why more Catholic school students didn't become nuns.
question.text: Name this eponymous initiative placed on the California ballot in 1978, which would have declared teachers who engaged in "public homosexual activity" to be "unfit for service."

swap.text: This associate Justice of the Supreme Court would hold the Ambassadorship from 1965 until 1968, following the tenure of Adlai Stevenson. He is best known today for authoring the majority opinion in Griswold v. Connecticut.
